aesthetic: Interference Pattern — A high-voltage Swiss-brutalist system inspired by the physics of wave interference. Two fundamental forces (human thought and mechanical computation) overlap throughout history, creating bright maxima where they reinforce and dark nulls where they cancel. The visual language is deliberately confrontational: extreme typographic scale, aggressive asymmetry, chromatic tension between warmth (the human, the Enlightenment) and cold (the machine, the modern). Rejects editorial safety in favor of poster-scale graphic impact. Every slide should feel like it could be ripped from a Weingart/Hofmann exhibition and hung on a concrete wall.
chromaticArc: Opens on Void (#0B0B0F) with a single massive title in Emission white — the deck begins in darkness, a signal emerging from nothing. Slide 2 (definition) explodes into Emission ground with Void type — the first clarity. Slides 3-4 (cybernetics vs AI) use split compositions: conceptually, Void and Emission fighting for dominance, with a Resonance red divider — the two waves meeting. Slide 5 (Longue Duree) returns to Emission with Phosphor accents — the Enlightenment warmth entering. Slides 6-14 (fundamental processes, proto-computing, deep history) alternate between Deep Frequency backgrounds for excavation and Emission grounds for analysis — the interference pattern oscillating. Crawford's quote (slide 10) gets full Void background with Resonance left-bar — maximum voltage for the most important passage. The feudalism/capitalism pair uses dramatic contrast. The grand timeline (slide 14) uses Deep Frequency with luminous Emission type and Patina table rules. Ballistics section (slides 15-20) introduces Phosphor accents heavily — these are the spark moments, the calculations that create weapons. Slides 21-22 (fundamentals/proposition) use Emission with bold Void typography. The contemporary section (slides 24-29) returns to Emission grounds with cool Interference gray accents — the present is less certain, more washed out. Education slides (30-35) use alternating Emission/Void with Resonance marking the crisis points. Final slide resolves on Void with a single Phosphor accent — an unresolved signal fading into the future.
gridStrategy: 60-column grid pushed to extremes. Standard slides: titles anchored hard-left at columns 2-3, spanning only 30-36 columns — leaving massive negative space on the right that acts as visual breathing room and counterweight. Body text set in narrow columns (span 28-32) offset from the title — never centered, always tensioned against the margin. Section breaks: title placed at vertical center but pushed far right (columns 28-56) — the asymmetry IS the statement. Split layouts for thematic dualities: hard column-30 divide with a 4px Resonance rule. Dense slides (timeline table): full 60 columns with dramatic type-scale contrast between headers and cells. Quotation slides: text compressed to columns 12-48 with enormous vertical margins, the emptiness carrying as much meaning as the words. Image-dominant slides: images span one half, text floats on the other with no attempt to balance — the imbalance IS the composition. Bottom: slide number at column 57, Interference gray.

fontStrategy.default: Helvetica Neue — the foundational Swiss grotesque, used for body text at 15px/1.55. Its neutrality is the point: the content speaks, not the font. Body text set at weight 400 to create maximum contrast with title weight.
fontStrategy.secondary: Helvetica Neue Bold/Black — the same face at extreme weights (700-800) for titles. No serif/sans pairing — this is a monofont system where ALL hierarchy comes from scale, weight, and position. Titles range from 36px (dense slides) to 52px (section openers). The absence of a second typeface forces the grid and color to do the structural work.
fontStrategy.tertiary: Courier New — used ONLY for dates, mathematical expressions, and the grand timeline. Its monospace register reads as 'data' against the proportional Helvetica, creating a visual code-switch between discourse and evidence.
fontStrategy.secondarySlides: On section openers, Helvetica Neue is set at 48-52px, weight 800, uppercase, tracking +0.08em — these titles function as posters within the deck. On the proposition slide, text is set at 28px, weight 300, tracking +0.02em — the thinness makes the bold claim feel more fragile and therefore more honest.

accentStrategy: Resonance red (#D62B1F) is used as a 4px vertical rule on exactly 6 slides — the moments of maximum intellectual friction (cybernetics vs AI, Crawford quote, Marx quote, ballistics origin, the proposition, education crisis). It appears at column 1, spanning full height — a siren stripe. Phosphor gold (#D4940A) appears as a 2px horizontal rule above titles on the Enlightenment/historical slides — the thread of rational light. Deep Frequency (#1A2E5A) as full-bleed background on max 5 slides — reserved for deepest historical excavation and the grand timeline. Patina green (#2B5E4A) structures tables: 1px horizontal rules between rows, no vertical rules — the table is read as layered strata. Interference gray (#6B6B6B) is the workhorse: section labels, bottom rules, footnote references. No decorative elements. No dots, no circles, no blocks. The only permitted accent shapes are horizontal rules, vertical rules, and full-bleed color. Mondrian-level austere.
